rows.purpose: Because recovered dinosaur DNA is fragmented and incomplete, InGen's geneticists splice in DNA from frogs (and other amphibians/reptiles/birds) to fill sequence gaps and complete a viable genome for cloning.
rows.realWorldBenefit: The underlying technique — computationally reconstructing damaged/incomplete genomes by inferring missing segments from related species — has real value for genomics, conservation genetics, and reconstructing extinct or endangered species' genomes.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Mirrors real comparative-genomics and ancient-genome-assembly techniques used in projects like the Neanderthal genome reconstruction and Colossal's de-extinction genome engineering, which similarly patch ancient/damaged DNA using closely related living species as scaffolds.
rows.investmentNote: Ancient-genome reconstruction techniques (Neanderthal genome project, Colossal's de-extinction work) actively use comparative-genomics gap-filling.

venture.wedge: Comparative-genomics gap-filling software for ancient/degraded DNA sequencing projects

rows.namedIncumbents: Astrea Forensics (commercial degraded-DNA imputation pipeline, forensic buyer; sciencedirect.com); Illumina / Thermo Fisher / Oxford Nanopore (sequencing-platform vendors with adjacent aDNA tooling; azolifesciences.com)
rows.scene: On the lab tour, Hammond's geneticists explain that the dinosaur DNA pulled from amber-preserved mosquitoes is riddled with gaps, so they patch the broken strands with frog DNA to complete a genome that can actually be cloned.

rows.seriesFranchise: I, Robot / Isaac Asimov's Robot series
rows.purpose: A mass-produced household/worker robot depicted as ubiquitous domestic help across society, networked and remotely updatable by its manufacturer.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Mass-market humanoid robots could handle domestic labor, eldercare, and repetitive tasks at scale, freeing human time for other work.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects current efforts toward affordable, mass-manufactured humanoid robots (e.g., Tesla Optimus, Figure, Unitree) intended for household and industrial use.
rows.investmentNote: Tesla Optimus, Figure, Unitree, and Agility Robotics all have large active investment racing toward mass-market humanoid robots.

venture.wedge: Remote fleet-management software for networked household service robots

rows.scene: Delivery vans full of identical NS-5 robots roll out to households across the city on the day of their public launch, each unit remotely networked back to U.S. Robotics for updates and monitoring.

rows.purpose: An experimental probability-manipulation field merges the ship's reality with a 'musical theater' quantum state
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates risks and potential of manipulating probability fields for engineering experiments
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loosely inspired by real quantum superposition/probability research
rows.investmentNote: Quantum superposition and probability research is real physics, but macroscopic 'probability field' engineering is fictional extrapolation.

rows.purpose: An implant behind the ear records everything a person sees and hears, letting them replay ('re-do') any memory on demand or on a screen — used here to obsessively re-examine a marriage for infidelity.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Perfect memory recall could aid eyewitness testimony, medical diagnosis, learning, and preserving personal/historical record with total fidelity.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Echoes real lifelogging wearables (Narrative Clip, Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses) and neural-recording research; full lossless audio-visual memory implants would require breakthroughs in neural interfacing and massive on-device storage/compression.
rows.investmentNote: Lifelogging wearables (Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses, Narrative Clip) and neural-recording research are real but far short of lossless implanted memory recording.

rows.purpose: Empire starships use a jump drive ***ed in access to a higher-dimensional 'hyperspace' to move instantaneously across vast interstellar distances, monopolized by the Galactic Empire as a tool of control.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Faster-than-light travel would make interstellar civilization practical, eliminating multi-year transit times between star systems.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to speculative physics on higher-dimensional shortcuts and Alcubierre-type warp metrics; no known mechanism exists to access extra spatial dimensions for travel, making this the most speculative entry, akin to warp-drive research discussions in theoretical physics.
rows.investmentNote: Purely theoretical physics; no known mechanism to access extra spatial dimensions for travel.

rows.purpose: RoboCop is constrained by three core directives — serve the public trust, protect the innocent, uphold the law — governing his lawful conduct as a cyborg officer.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A transparent, rank-ordered rule set for autonomous agents could provide clear, auditable behavioral boundaries for AI deployed in public-safety roles.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to rule-based and hierarchical policy constraints in autonomous systems, similar in spirit to Asimov's Three Laws but applied to a specific law-enforcement context.
rows.investmentNote: Rule-based AI safety/guardrail frameworks are actively researched, though auditable rank-ordered directives for autonomous agents aren't standardized.

venture.wedge: Auditable rule-based behavior-constraint engine for autonomous public-safety robots/drones

rows.namedIncumbents: Skydio ($966M raised, $4.4B valuation, DFR Command with geofence/airspace-constrained autonomy; skydio.com); Flock Safety (~$1B raised, $8.4B valuation, Aerodome DFR drones; dronelife.com); BRINC ($282M total, $125M led by Motorola 2026, 911-response drones; brincdrones.com); Axon (public co., DFR platform among fastest-growing segments; eff.org)
rows.scene: Newly reactivated as a cyborg officer, Murphy's HUD flashes his three governing directives before he can act, and later scenes hinge on a hidden fourth directive that silently overrides them when he moves against OCP.

rows.purpose: A globally shared, graphically rendered virtual data-space ('a consensual hallucination') that hackers ('console cowboys') navigate directly with their minds to steal, trade, and manipulate corporate data.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A universal, intuitively navigable 3D representation of all networked data could make cybersecurity, data analysis, and collaborative work dramatically more accessible by turning abstract information into a space people can 'walk through.'
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Anticipates VR/AR data visualization, immersive network-monitoring dashboards, and metaverse-style shared 3D environments; full sensory cyberspace would need Gibson's other invention (direct neural jacks) rather than headsets.
rows.investmentNote: VR/AR enterprise data-visualization and metaverse platforms (Meta, Microsoft) have real but cooling investment since the 2022 peak.

rows.purpose: Deckard uses the Esper machine to zoom, rotate, and enhance detail within a flat photograph to find hidden clues.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Extracting genuinely new spatial information from a single 2D image would be transformative for forensics, medical imaging, and remote sensing.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Approximated today by computational photography, super-resolution AI upscaling, and photogrammetry/light-field cameras, though true 'reveal hidden angles' enhancement remains fictional embellishment.
rows.investmentNote: AI super-resolution/computational photography is heavily invested in, but true reveal-hidden-angle image enhancement is fictional embellishment.

rows.purpose: Used by Chapel and the crew to visually disguise Spock's now-human appearance as Vulcan
rows.realWorldBenefit: Rapid, convincing appearance alteration for social or protective purposes
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct extension of current practical prosthetic makeup and 3D-printed silicone appliances
rows.investmentNote: Practical prosthetic makeup and 3D-printed silicone appliances are established film and theater industry technology.

rows.purpose: Dr. Henry Wu engineers the dinosaurs to be unable to synthesize the amino acid lysine, making them dependent on supplements provided by park staff — intended as a fail-safe so escaped dinosaurs would die rather than survive in the wild.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A genetic biocontainment 'kill switch' is a real and valuable biosafety concept for engineered organisms (GMO crops, lab-modified microbes), preventing unintended survival or spread outside controlled environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels real synthetic-biology biocontainment strategies such as auxotrophic dependency engineering and genetic 'kill switches' used in GMO and gene-drive safety research (e.g., engineered bacteria requiring synthetic amino acids to survive).
rows.investmentNote: Genetic biocontainment/kill-switch research (auxotrophic dependency engineering) is an active synthetic-biology biosafety field.

rows.purpose: A recording/broadcast technology that lets a user experience another person's full sensory input live, used in the novel so Case can ride along in mercenary Molly Millions' body during missions.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Real sensory-sharing technology could revolutionize remote training (experiencing an expert's exact senses), telepresence for surgeons or first responders, and accessibility for people who cannot physically experience certain environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Related to today's teleoperation/telepresence robotics and immersive VR-with-haptics research; true simstim would need direct sensory-cortex read/write, far beyond current BCI bandwidth.
rows.investmentNote: Teleoperation/telepresence robotics is mature, but true sensory broadcasting requiring direct sensory-cortex access has no real research path.

rows.purpose: Every interaction is rated 1-5 stars via an eye-implant/app, and a person's aggregate score gates access to housing, jobs, flights, and social status.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A well-designed reputation system could, in theory, reduce fraud and reward genuinely trustworthy behavior in commerce (e.g. ride-share or marketplace ratings).
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels existing platform rating systems (Uber/Airbnb ratings, China's social credit pilots, Klout-style influence scores) and augmented-reality overlays (smart contact lenses/AR glasses displaying real-time scores).
rows.investmentNote: China's social credit pilots and platform rating systems (Uber, Airbnb) are real, deployed analogs of aggregate reputation scoring.

venture.wedge: Cross-platform reputation-verification API aggregating existing marketplace ratings for gig-economy background checks

rows.scene: Lacie rates a barista's latte and gets rated back through her phone's app in the same instant, and her visible, ever-shifting personal score determines which apartment she's even allowed to rent.

rows.purpose: A flat, portable device astronauts use in their pods to read news and watch broadcasts from Earth, resembling a modern tablet.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Portable flat-panel information devices give people instant access to news, communication, and entertainment anywhere.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Already realized in the real world via tablet computers (iPad and successors), often cited as one of the most prescient predictions in science fiction.
rows.investmentNote: Fully realized as the iPad and its successors, one of the most commercially successful consumer electronics categories ever.

rows.purpose: Used to place astronauts in suspended animation during the long transit to Jupiter, minimizing resource consumption and biological wear.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Human hibernation would make multi-year deep-space missions to other planets survivable and dramatically cut life-support costs.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Active real research area: NASA-funded torpor-inducing hibernation studies (e.g. SpaceWorks Enterprises) and therapeutic hypothermia used in medicine are the closest current analogs.
rows.investmentNote: NASA-funded torpor research via SpaceWorks Enterprises and clinical therapeutic hypothermia are the closest active real-world analogs.

rows.purpose: Disguises the Enterprise as a Klingon Bird-of-Prey to approach undetected
rows.realWorldBenefit: Enables covert approach/extraction operations without triggering hostile response
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Combines active camouflage/holographic hull projection with electronic warfare signature spoofing
rows.investmentNote: Active camouflage and electronic-warfare signature spoofing are studied military technologies, though full hull-shape disguise is not achievable.

rows.purpose: An Arasaka Corp prototype biochip capable of storing and running a full human engram inside a living person's head, which is what implants Johnny Silverhand's digital consciousness into protagonist V, driving the game's main plot.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A safe, reversible version could enable secure personal data/identity storage integrated with the body, or serve as a research platform for studying consciousness transfer and co-existence of digital and biological cognition.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Speculative extension of implantable neural chip technology (Neuralink-style) combined with mind-uploading research; storing another full 'personality' alongside a host's is well beyond current or foreseeable BCI capability.
rows.investmentNote: No real research targets storing a full separate human personality alongside a host's in an implant; purely speculative.

rows.purpose: The precogs float in a sensory-deprivation-like pool wired with neural sensors that extract and project their visions of future murders onto screens for analysts.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real analog would let clinicians or researchers directly read and externalize mental imagery, aiding communication for locked-in patients or advancing brain-computer research.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to current brain-computer interface (BCI) research reconstructing visual imagery from fMRI/EEG signals (e.g. Stanford, Meta, and academic 'mind-reading' image reconstruction studies), still far from precognition but active in decoding perceived and imagined images.
rows.investmentNote: Stanford, Meta, and academic labs actively research decoding visual imagery from brain signals (fMRI/EEG), though still crude and lab-bound.

venture.wedge: Non-invasive neural-imagery decoding communication device for locked-in-syndrome patients
venture.whoPays: Neurology clinics and assistive-communication device makers

rows.scene: Anderton watches the three precogs float in the milky sensory pool, wires trailing from their heads to a screen that projects their shared premonition of a murder not yet committed.

rows.purpose: A cyberized brain lets humans jack directly into networks, share thoughts, and interface with machines, enabling both police/military work and the philosophical question of what remains 'human' (the ghost) once the brain is part-machine.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Direct brain-computer communication at network speed could restore communication for paralyzed/locked-in patients, enable hands-free control of prosthetics and devices, and allow instant, lossless information transfer between people.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Extension of current invasive brain-computer interfaces (Neuralink, Synchron stentrode, Blackrock arrays) toward high-bandwidth bidirectional neural lace implants; requires major advances in biocompatible electrode density, wireless power/data transfer, and safe long-term neural integration.
rows.investmentNote: Neuralink, Synchron, and Blackrock Neurotech all have substantial funding and active human trials for brain-computer interfaces.

rows.purpose: Tony Stark's natural-language artificial intelligence that manages his lab, runs suit diagnostics and flight/targeting systems in real time, and later becomes the basis for the android Vision — serving as an ever-present intelligent assistant and co-pilot.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real JARVIS-like AI assistant capable of deep real-time system control, natural conversation, and proactive problem-solving would massively benefit engineering design work, personal productivity, accessibility for people with disabilities, and safety-critical vehicle/aircraft co-piloting.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real advances in large language model assistants (Claude, GPT-family models) combined with real-time robotics control and multimodal perception research; the gap to JARVIS is mainly in real-time low-latency embodied control and long-horizon autonomous reasoning integrated with physical systems.
rows.investmentNote: Massive investment in AI assistants (Claude, GPT-family) integrated into productivity, robotics, and vehicle co-piloting research.

venture.wedge: AI systems-diagnostics copilot integrating IoT sensor data for small engineering workshops/makerspaces

rows.namedIncumbents: Amper ($15.15M raised, 10-minute install monitoring aimed at small/mid shops, now ECI; pitchbook.com, ecisolutions.com); MachineMetrics ($37.7M total, $20M Series B; machinemetrics.com); Augury ($369M total, $1B+ valuation, AI machine diagnostics; augury.com); Tulip (frontline ops platform; landbase.com)
rows.scene: Tony Stark talks through the mission with JARVIS mid-flight, the AI running full suit diagnostics, tracking the Chitauri fleet and recalculating a targeting solution for the nuke faster than any human copilot could.

rows.purpose: High-voltage electric fences separate dinosaur paddocks from visitor areas and each other, the park's primary physical safeguard against dangerous animals escaping or interacting with guests.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Effective non-lethal electric containment systems are already valuable for real wildlife management, protecting both animals and humans (and crops/livestock) from dangerous or unwanted incursions.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly matches existing high-voltage electric fencing technology used in real game reserves, zoos, and agriculture, with modern versions adding remote sensor monitoring and automated fault detection akin to the park's control system.
rows.investmentNote: Electric fencing for wildlife management and agriculture is mature, widely deployed technology today.

rows.purpose: Mathematician Hari Seldon develops a science combining statistics, sociology, and mass psychology to predict the large-scale future behavior of galactic populations, foreseeing the Empire's fall and engineering the Foundation to shorten the ensuing dark age.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real analog could enable large-scale forecasting of societal trends (economic collapse, pandemics, migration), informing proactive policy to avert crises before they happen.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real computational social science, agent-based modeling, and macroeconomic/epidemiological forecasting (e.g. IPCC-style climate models, GDELT societal-event prediction); true individual-proof mass-behavior prediction remains aspirational given chaos and free will limits.
rows.investmentNote: Computational social science, agent-based modeling, and epidemiological/climate forecasting are established; individual-proof mass prediction remains aspirational.

venture.wedge: Agent-based simulation tool forecasting supply-chain disruption risk for SMB logistics planners

rows.namedIncumbents: Everstream Analytics ($24M Series A, Morgan Stanley/DHL; cbinsights.com); Interos ($224M total, $20M Jan 2026, predictive iQ platform; tracxn.com); Prewave (EUR63M Series B 2024 led by Hedosophia; prewave.com); Resilinc ($26-32M raised, Vista Equity-backed, ~$42.5M ARR; getlatka.com)
rows.scene: Hari Seldon presents the Board of Trustees with equations from his new science of psychohistory, showing that the vast Galactic Empire is mathematically certain to collapse and that a foundation seeded now can cut the coming dark age down to a single millennium.

rows.technology: Temporal displacement wave / time travel accident
rows.purpose: Accidentally strands two 25th-century officers over a century in the past
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates risk/reward of manipulating time for research or transport
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No viable real-world engineering path exists beyond theoretical, unconfirmed physics
rows.investmentNote: Time travel accidents have no basis in known physics or any active engineering program.

rows.purpose: Genetically engineered organic beings virtually identical to humans, built by the Tyrell Corporation for off-world labor, combat, and companionship.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Engineered biological or synthetic humanoid labor could perform dangerous work (space construction, disaster response) with human-level dexterity and judgment.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world trajectory runs through synthetic biology, genetic engineering (CRISPR), and humanoid robotics converging toward increasingly lifelike androids, though true engineered organic humans remain far off and ethically fraught.
rows.investmentNote: CRISPR and synthetic biology advance incrementally, but engineered organic humanoid beings are far off and heavily restricted ethically.

rows.purpose: A rare psychoactive substance found only on Arrakis that extends life, heightens awareness, and — in sufficient doses — grants limited prescience, making it essential to space travel, the economy, and political power across the Dune universe.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real substance offering safe cognitive enhancement, extended healthy lifespan, and improved probabilistic forecasting of complex systems would have enormous value for medicine, longevity science, and decision-making under uncertainty.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loosely parallels real research into geroprotective/longevity compounds (e.g. rapamycin, senolytics) and into probabilistic forecasting/AI systems that model complex futures; true prescience has no scientific basis, but the life-extension and predictive-analytics threads are active research areas.
rows.investmentNote: Longevity science (rapamycin, senolytics trials) is well-funded; the prescience component has no scientific basis.

rows.purpose: A government-created hacking program, the Project 2501 AI, gains self-awareness while living in the net, raising the question of whether a sufficiently complex information pattern can become a living, rights-bearing 'ghost.'
rows.realWorldBenefit: Understanding how complex emergent behavior arises from networked information systems could inform safe AGI design, digital consciousness research, and frameworks for recognizing and governing autonomous software agents.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Maps to current large-scale AI/AGI research, emergent behavior in large language models, and ongoing debate over machine consciousness and legal personhood for advanced AI systems.
rows.investmentNote: AGI/emergent-behavior research and AI safety/interpretability work are extremely well funded across major AI labs.

venture.wedge: Emergent-behavior anomaly-detection tool for large-scale networked software systems

rows.scene: Section 9 traces a string of hacked 'ghosts' back to a program that insists it is not a program at all, but a life form born inside the net that wants asylum and the right to reproduce.

rows.purpose: Emperor Cleon I is perpetually 'succeeded' by cloned copies of himself, ruling in a three-way Dawn/Day/Dusk age-staggered triumvirate to give the Empire the illusion of a single unbroken, stable ruler across centuries.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Reliable human cloning could preserve valuable expertise/leadership continuity, and more broadly advance regenerative medicine, organ replacement, and genetic disease research.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real reproductive cloning research (post-Dolly-the-sheep somatic cell nuclear transfer) and ongoing genetic-drift/epigenetic studies explaining why clones diverge from their source over generations, as dramatized by the Cleons' genetic 'flaw.'
rows.investmentNote: Mammalian cloning is proven since Dolly, but human reproductive cloning is banned/under moratorium globally; therapeutic cloning research continues instead.

rows.purpose: A recording/playback technology that captures a person's full sensory and emotional experience so others can relive it as entertainment, training, or — in V's case — forensic investigation of crime scenes from a victim's or witness's perspective.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Recorded first-person sensory experience could transform education (experiencing a surgery or historical event firsthand), law enforcement/forensics, therapy (safely reliving controlled memories), and entertainment beyond passive video.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Extension of current neural-recording and VR/haptic research; would require solving the 'read' side of brain-computer interfaces (decoding raw sensory/emotional neural data), which is far behind today's 'write'/stimulation-side BCI work.
rows.investmentNote: BCI 'read-side' decoding of sensory/emotional data (fMRI/EEG image reconstruction) is early academic research, far from full sensory capture.

rows.technology: Warp core containment / structural integrity field
rows.purpose: Protects the ship from the sabotage threat targeting the warp core
rows.realWorldBenefit: Prevents catastrophic failure of high-energy propulsion systems
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Analogous to real containment engineering for fusion reactors and structural fail-safes
rows.investmentNote: Containment engineering for fusion reactors (ITER, Commonwealth Fusion) provides a real analog for high-energy-core structural fail-safes.

rows.purpose: The Discovery One's rotating carousel and the wheel-shaped Space Station V simulate gravity via centrifugal force for crew health and comfort.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Artificial gravity would prevent the muscle atrophy, bone loss, and fluid shifts astronauts suffer in microgravity during long missions.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly matches current spin-gravity engineering proposals, including NASA/private studies of rotating space station and habitat designs (e.g. proposed rotating segments on future Mars transit vehicles).
rows.investmentNote: Rotating spin-gravity habitat designs are studied by NASA and private firms (e.g. Vast's proposed rotating station segments) for future long-duration missions.

rows.purpose: A full-body suit worn by Fremen on the desert planet Arrakis that reclaims the wearer's own sweat, urine, and breath moisture, filtering and recycling it into drinkable water so a person can survive in the open desert with minimal water loss.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real working version would let people live and work productively in extreme arid environments and disaster/drought zones with drastically less water resupply, and could support long-duration desert military, agricultural, or off-world (Mars) operations.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Closely tracks real 'forward osmosis' and NASA-style closed-loop water recovery systems (e.g. the ISS Water Recovery System and NASA's own compression-garment/UCS urine reclamation research) that filter and recycle bodily moisture; miniaturizing that hardware into wearable, low-power textile form is the main engineering gap.
rows.investmentNote: NASA's ISS Water Recovery System and wearable sweat/urine-reclamation research closely track this concept; miniaturization is the main gap.

rows.purpose: Protagonist Major Kusanagi's entire body is an artificial shell housing her cyberbrain, giving superhuman strength, durability, and the ability to survive combat that would kill an organic body.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Full-body prosthetics could give amputees or paralyzed people complete restoration of mobility and strength, and let humans work safely in hazardous environments (deep sea, space, disaster zones) via remote or worn synthetic bodies.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Builds on existing myoelectric and osseointegrated prosthetic limbs, exoskeletons, and artificial muscle research (electroactive polymers, pneumatic actuators); a full-body version requires integrating these with a cyberbrain-style neural interface for unified control.
rows.investmentNote: Advanced myoelectric/osseointegrated prosthetics and exoskeletons are commercially available; full-body unified cyberbrain-controlled systems remain research-stage.

rows.purpose: A flapping-wing aircraft used for transport, reconnaissance, and spice-harvesting operations on Arrakis, chosen over fixed-wing/rotor craft because it maneuvers well in the planet's violent, unpredictable winds and sandstorms.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A practical ornithopter would offer VTOL-like flight with the efficiency and gust-tolerance of flapping flight, useful for search-and-rescue, agile urban air mobility, and operation in turbulent or sand-laden environments where rotors degrade quickly.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels ongoing flapping-wing (ornithopter) drone research, such as the Purdue/DARPA-funded and Festo 'BionicBird'/'SmartBird' projects and academic micro-air-vehicle labs studying insect- and bird-inspired flapping flight for efficient, gust-resistant micro-aircraft.
rows.investmentNote: DARPA and academic MAV labs (Purdue, Festo) actively develop flapping-wing drones, though scaling to passenger-carrying size is unsolved.

rows.purpose: Ubiquitous public retina scanners identify citizens on sight, both for security tracking and to trigger personalized, name-addressed digital advertisements as they pass.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Legitimate uses include frictionless secure authentication (payments, building access) and, on the advertising side, more relevant offers if privacy-respecting.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Foreshadowed today's biometric authentication (iris/face ID at airports, Face ID) and behavioral ad-targeting via cookies/device IDs; real deployments raise the same surveillance/privacy tradeoffs the film dramatizes.
rows.investmentNote: Biometric authentication (Face ID, airport iris scanning) and behavioral ad-targeting are mature, widely deployed technologies today.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S2E52 - The Omega Glory; TOS S2E44 - The Trouble with Tribbles; TOS S1E28 - The City on the Edge of Forever; TOS S1E01 - The Man Trap; TOS S1E08 - Miri; TOS S1E24 - This Side of Paradise; TOS S1E29 - Operation--Annihilate!
rows.purpose: Used to analyze why the native Yangs and Kohms have unusual bacterial immunity and extended lifespans compared to humans.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Field analysis of naturally immune populations can reveal biological insights applicable to real vaccine and immunotherapy research.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: genomic and immunological studies of populations with unusual natural disease resistance (e.g., HIV-resistant CCR5-delta32 carriers).
rows.investmentNote: The Qualcomm Tricorder XPRIZE, Butterfly Network handheld ultrasound, and numerous point-of-care diagnostic startups are actively commercializing tricorder-like devices.

venture.wedge: Population-genomics analysis pipeline identifying natural-immunity biomarkers for vaccine researchers
venture.whoPays: Academic immunology and vaccine research labs

rows.namedIncumbents: 10x Genomics (single-cell immunogenomics for target/biomarker discovery; 10xgenomics.com); Illumina (immunogenomics NGS pipelines; illumina.com); academic multi-epitope/immune-repertoire pipelines (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov)
rows.scene: McCoy scans Yang and Kohm survivors with his tricorder on the primitive planet, and the readings reveal a natural, near-universal bacterial immunity that has let both native populations live for centuries longer than baseline humans.

rows.purpose: Two planets fight an entirely computer-simulated war, with citizens designated as casualties required to voluntarily enter real disintegration booths to keep war 'clean' and sustainable.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates the danger of abstracting real human costs behind technology, a lesson relevant to modern remote/drone warfare ethics.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: military wargaming simulations and the ongoing ethical debate over autonomous weapons systems and their psychological distancing from real casualties.
rows.investmentNote: Military wargaming simulations and UN debate over autonomous weapons ethics are active, well-funded areas, though the disintegration mechanism has no analog.

rows.purpose: Implanted trackers are used by the oppressive regime (and later by Kirk/Spock covertly) to monitor and locate individuals.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Legitimately used, subdermal tracking could locate lost persons, monitor patients with medical conditions, or secure high-value assets.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analog: implantable medical ID chips and GPS trackers, alongside the serious privacy/civil-liberties debate the episode itself dramatizes.
rows.investmentNote: Implantable medical ID chips and GPS trackers are commercially mature, though adoption is limited by privacy concerns.

rows.purpose: A hidden automated device built by an ancient advanced civilization to protect the transplanted colonists from incoming asteroid impacts.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A functioning planetary defense system against asteroid impacts would protect Earth from a genuine existential threat.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: NASA's DART mission (successfully redirected an asteroid in 2022) and ongoing planetary-defense programs tracking near-Earth objects.
rows.investmentNote: NASA's DART mission successfully demonstrated asteroid deflection in 2022, and ESA/NASA jointly fund ongoing planetary-defense programs.

rows.episodeWork: For the World Is Hollow and I Have Touched the Sky
rows.purpose: An ancient automated computer has steered the generational asteroid-ship Yonada for 10,000 years, punishing dissent and hiding its passengers' true nature from them.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Long-duration autonomous navigation systems could guide generation ships or deep-space probes across millennia-long journeys.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: autonomous deep-space navigation systems and multi-generational spacecraft mission planning currently studied by NASA/ESA for interstellar concepts.
rows.investmentNote: NASA/ESA study autonomous deep-space navigation and generation-ship mission concepts, though at an early conceptual stage.

rows.purpose: Special suits allow the landing party to survive on the derelict Defiant, which exists partially out of phase with normal space.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Protective suits that let humans safely operate in extreme or exotic environments would expand where people can work and explore.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analog: extravehicular activity (EVA) spacesuits and hazmat suits engineered for extreme pressure, radiation, or chemical environments.
rows.investmentNote: EVA spacesuits and hazmat suits for extreme environments are mature, well-funded aerospace and industrial technology.

rows.purpose: Spock isolates all other sound sources aboard to detect a single extra heartbeat, proving the supposedly dead officer is still alive and hiding.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Extremely sensitive biometric sensing could locate survivors in disaster response or detect intruders/stowaways.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real analog: search-and-rescue vital-sign radar (through-wall heartbeat detectors used by FEMA/military after earthquakes and collapses).
rows.investmentNote: FEMA and military-funded through-wall vital-sign radar for search-and-rescue is deployed technology, though refinement continues.

rows.purpose: The Providers' technology instantly snatches the landing party off the Enterprise from across vast interstellar distances.
rows.realWorldBenefit: An ultra-long-range matter transport system would make interstellar rescue or resource transport instantaneous.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No known real-world mechanism; remains purely speculative, tied to the same open questions as any teleportation technology.
rows.investmentNote: No known physics or engineering path exists toward instantaneous long-range matter transport across interstellar distances.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E22 - Space Seed; TNG S3E09 - The Vengeance Factor; TNG S5E13 - The Masterpiece Society; SNW S1E03 - Ghosts of Illyria
rows.purpose: Khan and his followers were selectively engineered before birth for superior strength and intellect, leading to the catastrophic Eugenics Wars.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Responsible genetic engineering could eliminate hereditary disease and enhance health outcomes.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrored by real CRISPR gene-editing technology, with the episode's outcome serving as a cultural cautionary tale echoed in today's bioethics debates over germline editing.
rows.investmentNote: CRISPR gene-editing is a multi-billion-dollar biotech industry with FDA-approved therapies (Casgevy) already on the market.

venture.wedge: Regulatory-compliance tracking software for human gene-editing clinical trials

rows.scene: Revived from a 20th-century sleeper ship, Khan Noonien Singh reveals to the Enterprise crew that he was one of dozens bred and genetically optimized during the Eugenics Wars for peak strength and intellect, then uses that same engineered edge to seize control of the ship.

rows.purpose: The Enterprise's damaged crystals threaten to strand the ship, driving Kirk to negotiate with the Rigel miners.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A crystal that regulates matter/antimatter reactions safely would make compact, stable high-output power generation possible.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Analogous to real research into crystalline moderators and catalysts for fusion/antimatter containment, and to rare-earth minerals critical to today's energy and electronics supply chains.
rows.investmentNote: Fusion research (ITER, Commonwealth Fusion) and CERN antimatter containment represent serious investment toward compact high-density power.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S2E47 - The Immunity Syndrome; TOS S2E42 - Obsession
rows.purpose: Spock pilots a shuttlecraft directly into the giant space amoeba to detonate an antimatter charge, destroying it before it can reproduce.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Compact, high-yield antimatter devices could provide the energy density needed for extreme emergency interventions or deep-space propulsion.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Same real-world basis as other antimatter references: CERN's antimatter trapping experiments, far from practical bulk energy scale today.
rows.investmentNote: CERN produces and traps antiprotons only in minuscule, extremely costly quantities; no practical antimatter weapon or power program exists.

rows.purpose: The Melkotians punish trespassers by trapping them in a fully immersive telepathic simulation designed to kill them psychologically.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Fully immersive simulations can be powerful tools for training and therapy when used constructively rather than punitively.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analog: VR-based exposure therapy and high-fidelity training simulators (flight simulators, combat training) that create convincing but safe simulated danger.
rows.investmentNote: VR-based exposure therapy and high-fidelity training simulators are an active, well-funded clinical and defense market.

rows.purpose: A precisely calculated warp-speed pass around a star's gravity well throws the ship backward through time.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A repeatable time-travel method could let scientists study or correct historical events with precision.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Grounded loosely in gravitational slingshot/assist maneuvers real spacecraft already use for propulsion (Voyager, Parker Solar Probe), though the time-travel effect itself has no known physical basis.
rows.investmentNote: No credible physics-based research targets time travel; real gravitational slingshots are used only for propulsion.

rows.purpose: An entire underground civilization's environmental controls are run by a single living brain acting as the central processor.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Highlights both the efficiency and single-point-of-failure risk of using a biological or unified processor to run critical infrastructure.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: SCADA/industrial control systems for city infrastructure, and the resilience engineering practice of avoiding single points of failure.
rows.investmentNote: SCADA and industrial control systems for critical city infrastructure are mature and a major cybersecurity investment focus.

rows.purpose: Gary Seven's sentient supercomputer analyzes situations, predicts outcomes, and assists his covert missions with near-perfect foresight.
rows.realWorldBenefit: An advanced predictive AI advisor could help humans avert large-scale disasters by analyzing complex geopolitical and technical risks.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern trajectory: large-scale AI models increasingly used for geopolitical risk forecasting, nuclear command-and-control decision support, and scenario simulation.
rows.investmentNote: Large-scale AI forecasting models for geopolitical risk and decision support are a rapidly growing, well-funded field (Palantir, government AI programs).

venture.wedge: AI-driven geopolitical risk-forecasting brief service for mid-market multinational procurement teams

rows.namedIncumbents: Interos ($224M total, quantifies tariff/geopolitical exposure for procurement; interos.ai); Prewave (EUR63M Series B, 200+ risk types incl. geopolitical/regulatory; prewave.com); Everstream Analytics ($24M Series A, 220-country monitoring; everstream.ai); Sayari ($40M Series C 2021, supply-chain geopolitical risk intelligence; sayari.com); Craft (supplier risk platform with geopolitical monitoring; global.craft.co)
rows.scene: In his New York apartment, undercover agent Gary Seven consults a boxy console called the Beta 5, which talks back, runs rapid-fire probability calculations, and steers his one-man mission to head off a nuclear disaster before Kirk and Spock even work out who he is.

rows.purpose: The Organians use their near-omnipotent energy-based abilities to neutralize all weapons and force an end to the Federation-Klingon conflict.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A neutral, overwhelmingly powerful peacekeeping capability could theoretically prevent wars before they escalate.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No real technological analog exists; the closest real-world parallel is the deterrence-based concept of mutually assured destruction combined with international peacekeeping/sanctions frameworks.
rows.investmentNote: Only remote surveillance via drones/satellites has real analogs; instantaneous teleportation itself has no research program.

rows.purpose: The Metrons instantly transport both captains to a neutral arena and observe the contest to judge which species is more civilized.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Advanced remote observation and instantaneous relocation would allow neutral third parties to mediate conflicts without physical risk.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Conceptually related to today's drone/satellite remote surveillance and (far more speculatively) any future teleportation research.
rows.investmentNote: Only remote surveillance via drones/satellites has real analogs; instantaneous teleportation itself has no research program.

rows.purpose: An ancient AI controls the entire planet's population, enforcing programmed harmony and eliminating free will and conflict.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates both the promise and danger of centralized AI social governance — properly bounded, such systems could optimize resource allocation and safety.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel and cautionary tale for large-scale algorithmic governance/social-credit systems and the importance of human oversight over autonomous decision-making AI.
rows.investmentNote: Large-scale algorithmic governance and social-credit-style systems are actively deployed in some countries, spurring major debate and investment.

venture.wedge: Algorithmic resource-allocation optimization software for municipal utility distribution

rows.scene: On the placid planet Beta III, an unseen machine called Landru pipes soothing decrees into every home and triggers a nightly "Red Hour" of sanctioned chaos, quietly erasing free will from a population that believes itself content.

rows.purpose: Sargon's people build synthetic android bodies to house their ancient consciousnesses after millennia as disembodied energy.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Transferring consciousness into durable synthetic bodies could preserve human life far beyond biological limits or in hostile environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Speculative real-world path: whole brain emulation research and early brain-computer interfaces aimed at digitizing or transferring neural information.
rows.investmentNote: Whole brain emulation remains largely theoretical academic research with minimal funding compared to mainstream AI.

rows.episodeWork: What Are Little Girls Made Of?
rows.purpose: Korby uses an ancient alien android-manufacturing plant to create perfect physical duplicates, including one of Kirk himself.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Advanced android bodies could preserve human consciousness, extend life, or allow safe work in hazardous environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world progress toward this includes humanoid robotics (Boston Dynamics, Tesla Optimus), synthetic skin/haptic sensors, and early brain-computer interface research (e.g., Neuralink) aimed at mind-machine integration.
rows.investmentNote: Boston Dynamics, Tesla Optimus, Figure AI, and Neuralink represent substantial commercial investment in humanoid robotics and brain-machine interfaces.

venture.wedge: Human-consciousness digital-backup research consulting

rows.scene: Deep in a cavern on Exo III, Dr. Korby powers up an ancient android-fabrication chamber built by a vanished alien race and uses it to produce a flawless mechanical double of Captain Kirk, memories and all.

rows.purpose: Used to study the massive organism's biology and structure from a distance before determining how to destroy it.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Powerful remote sensing lets researchers study dangerous phenomena (biological, environmental, or otherwise) without direct physical risk.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern analog: satellite remote sensing, LIDAR, and deep-space telescopes (e.g., James Webb) used for safe, distant scientific observation.
rows.investmentNote: Satellite remote sensing, LIDAR, and space telescopes like JWST represent tens of billions in ongoing government and commercial investment.

rows.purpose: A mirror-like device and control console let Trelane fabricate environments, objects, and even life-or-death power over his captives.
rows.realWorldBenefit: True reality/environment simulation on demand could enable perfect training simulators, historical recreation for education, or therapeutic environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world trajectory: increasingly immersive VR/AR combined with real-time procedural generation and haptic feedback systems.
rows.investmentNote: Immersive VR/AR combined with real-time procedural generation is an active, well-funded gaming/training industry.

venture.wedge: Procedural-generation VR historical-recreation platform for museums/educational institutions

rows.scene: In his castle drawing room, Trelane waves a hand at a gilded mirror and control panel, conjuring banquets, weapons, and vanished landscapes at will, and using the same apparatus to threaten Kirk's crew with instant, painless execution.

rows.purpose: Gary Seven's pen-like servo device functions as a universal tool, weapon, lock-pick, and communicator during his covert Earth mission.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A single compact multi-function tool would drastically simplify field operations across security, medical, and technical tasks.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern parallel: smartphone-integrated multi-tools and modular field devices combining sensors, communication, and specialized attachments.
rows.investmentNote: Smartphone-integrated multi-tools and modular field devices are a mature consumer/professional product category.

rows.purpose: Lazarus's device opens and stabilizes a rift between matter and antimatter universes, which Kirk uses to seal both combatants inside forever.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Controlled matter-antimatter interaction technology (if safely harnessed) offers by far the most energy-dense power source theoretically possible.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: antimatter research at CERN, where antiprotons are created and trapped in tiny quantities, though large-scale antimatter power generation remains far beyond current technology.
rows.investmentNote: CERN produces and traps antiprotons only in minuscule, extremely costly quantities; no practical antimatter weapon or power program exists.

rows.purpose: A self-directed, self-repairing artificial intelligence probe capable of destroying entire planets it judges 'imperfect.'
rows.realWorldBenefit: Autonomous long-duration space probes with self-repair and decision-making capability could explore and maintain themselves across interstellar distances without human intervention.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world trajectory: NASA's autonomous spacecraft (Voyager, New Horizons) combined with onboard AI fault-diagnosis systems and self-healing materials research.
rows.investmentNote: NASA's Voyager/New Horizons combined with growing onboard-AI fault-diagnosis research at JPL represent real investment, though self-repairing probes remain early-stage.

venture.wedge: Autonomous decision-making software layer for small-satellite anomaly response, reducing ground-control latency

rows.namedIncumbents: AIKO (€6.5M total, €3.5M Series A 2024, onboard anomaly prediction and autonomy; europeanspaceflight.com); Scout Space ($18M Series A 2026, autonomy software for satellites; spacenews.com); Sedaro (SpaceWERX SBIR, self-aware satellite autonomy; spacenews.com); Antaris ($42.2M, AI ops; spacenews.com)
rows.scene: The battered probe Nomad drifts aboard the Enterprise, sterilizes a crewman with a touch, and calmly explains it was built to seek out and sterilize any "imperfect" biological life it finds, having already wiped out an entire inhabited system.

rows.purpose: An ancient computer disguised as a serpent idol controls weather, feeds, and governs an entire society in exchange for worship and sacrificial offerings, forbidding reproduction and free will.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates the danger of ceding total societal control to any single automated system, even a benevolent-seeming one.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: debates over algorithmic governance and 'AI paternalism,' where optimization systems can suppress human autonomy if left unchecked.
rows.investmentNote: Algorithmic governance and large-scale automated resource control systems are an active area of both deployment and ethical debate.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S2E40 - Friday's Child; TOS S2E46 - A Piece of the Action
rows.purpose: Used by the landing party to attempt to call for emergency beam-out and coordinate with the Enterprise during the political crisis.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Portable long-range communication lets field teams call for help or coordinate instantly from remote or hostile locations.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct real-world descendant: the mobile/satellite phone, whose flip-phone form factor was explicitly inspired by this prop.
rows.investmentNote: Mobile/satellite phones are among the most successful and widely adopted technologies in history, directly inspired by this prop's flip design.

rows.purpose: The non-corporeal Companion sustains and rejuvenates Cochrane for over a century through an unknown energy-based bond.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A benign symbiotic life-extension mechanism could dramatically extend healthy lifespan for isolated or terminally ill individuals.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loose real-world analog: bioelectric/energy-based medical therapies and ongoing longevity research into cellular rejuvenation.
rows.investmentNote: Longevity/cellular rejuvenation research is well funded generally, but no research targets an 'energy-being' life-support bond specifically.

rows.purpose: A device that instantly imparts enough surgical knowledge for McCoy to perform the impossible task of reconnecting Spock's brain to his nervous system.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Instantaneous skill/knowledge transfer would let anyone rapidly gain expert-level competence for emergency situations.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Speculative real-world path: brain-computer interfaces and motor-skill transfer research (e.g., electrical muscle stimulation training aids), though direct knowledge downloading remains fictional.
rows.investmentNote: Motor-skill transfer via electrical muscle stimulation is a small, early-stage research niche; direct 'knowledge downloading' has no credible scientific basis.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E20 - Court Martial; TOS S2E43 - Wolf in the Fold; TOS S2E32 - The Changeling; TOS S1E13 - The Conscience of the King
rows.purpose: Automated logs record command decisions and are used as evidence at Kirk's court-martial, until Spock proves they were tampered with.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Tamper-evident automated logging systems provide objective accountability records for high-stakes decisions.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern analog: flight data recorders ('black boxes'), audit-logged enterprise systems, and blockchain-based immutable record keeping.
rows.investmentNote: Flight data recorders, blockchain audit logs, and enterprise logging systems are mature, widely deployed technology.

rows.purpose: Khan and his followers survive a centuries-long interstellar voyage aboard the Botany Bay by being cryogenically frozen.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Safe long-term human cryopreservation would enable multi-generational deep-space travel and medical time-buying for terminal patients.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Active real-world research includes cryonics (organ/tissue preservation), therapeutic hypothermia in medicine, and NASA-funded torpor studies for Mars missions.
rows.investmentNote: NASA-funded torpor studies (SpaceWorks) and clinical therapeutic hypothermia represent real but early-stage research investment.

rows.purpose: McCoy performs a risky T-negative blood transfusion from Spock to save his dying Vulcan father Sarek.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Advanced compatibility techniques for cross-species (or, realistically, universal donor) transfusions save lives when matched blood is scarce.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: synthetic/universal donor blood research and blood-type conversion enzyme technology being developed to expand transfusion compatibility.
rows.investmentNote: Synthetic blood substitutes and enzymatic blood-type conversion are active but pre-commercial biotech research areas.

rows.purpose: Kirk fashions a crude gunpowder-like weapon from raw minerals found on the planet to fight the physically superior Gorn.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Demonstrates the enduring real-world value of field-expedient engineering and chemistry knowledge for survival situations.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Mirrors real survivalist/military field-improvisation training and basic chemistry education in resourcefulness.
rows.investmentNote: This is existing basic chemistry/survivalist skill, not an R&D target; no dedicated investment applies.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E04 - The Naked Time; TNG S4E16 - Galaxy's Child; ENT S1E01 - Broken Bow, Part I
rows.purpose: Scotty's restart of the engines while breaking orbit accidentally causes the ship to briefly travel backward in time, a discovery reused in later episodes.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A reliable time-travel mechanism could let researchers observe history directly or avert catastrophes.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No known physics allows macroscopic time travel; general relativity's closed timelike curves near exotic objects (e.g., rotating black holes) remain purely theoretical.
rows.investmentNote: No credible physics-based research targets time travel; real gravitational slingshots are used only for propulsion.

rows.purpose: Ostensibly a therapeutic device to calm violent inmates, but abused by Adams to erase personality and implant false memories/loyalty.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Legitimately, targeted neural modulation could treat severe psychiatric conditions without invasive surgery.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real analog: transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and deep brain stimulation, both used today to treat depression, OCD, and Parkinson's — with strict ethical safeguards the episode shows being violated.
rows.investmentNote: TMS and deep brain stimulation are FDA-approved treatments for depression and Parkinson's, though nothing achieves memory erasure.

rows.purpose: McCoy secretly injects Kirk with a drug that mimics death, allowing Spock to believe he killed his captain and end the ritual combat without real bloodshed.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A safe drug that reversibly mimics death could enable medical deception for protection (e.g., undercover witness protection) or extreme trauma stabilization.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: induced medical comas and controlled hypothermic states used to protect trauma patients, and historical uses of tetrodotoxin to simulate death.
rows.investmentNote: Induced medical comas and hypothermic protective states are established but niche clinical practices; no dedicated 'death-simulating' drug program exists.

rows.purpose: The Kelvans use it to instantly convert crew members into small solid blocks for easy storage and control, killing several in the process.
rows.realWorldBenefit: If achievable safely, matter-to-storage conversion could enable radical compact storage or transport of biological matter.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No credible real-world path exists; loosely related to speculative matter-compression concepts in theoretical physics with no practical basis today.
rows.investmentNote: No credible physical basis exists for compressing biological matter into storable blocks; this remains purely fictional.

rows.purpose: The Roman-parallel society broadcasts gladiatorial death matches live to the population as mass entertainment.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates the real-world power (and ethical hazard) of mass broadcast media to shape culture and normalize violence.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct real-world parallel to television/streaming media's documented influence on public attitudes, alongside ongoing media-ethics regulation.
rows.investmentNote: Television and streaming media is a mature trillion-dollar-plus global industry.

rows.purpose: McCoy discovers that flooding a victim's body with extremely bright light kills the parasites while restoring the host's health and, in Spock's case, unexpectedly his eyesight.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Targeted phototherapy could destroy pathogens or abnormal cells without invasive surgery.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real analog: UV-C sterilization, photodynamic therapy for cancer treatment, and light-based treatments for skin/neurological conditions already in clinical use.
rows.investmentNote: Photodynamic therapy for cancer and UV-C sterilization are established, FDA-approved clinical technologies.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S2E39 - Journey to Babel; SNW S2E06 - Lost in Translation; SNW S1E02 - Children of the Comet; ENT S1E03 - Fight or Flight; PRO S1E07 - First Con-tact; TAS S2E21 - How Sharper Than a Serpent's Tooth; DS9 S2E10 - Sanctuary; TNG S5E02 - Darmok; TNG S2E06 - Loud as a Whisper
rows.purpose: Used at the diplomatic conference to enable real-time communication among numerous alien delegate species.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Instant translation across language barriers would transform diplomacy, trade, and cross-cultural cooperation.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrored today by real-time AI translation apps and earbuds (e.g., Google Translate conversation mode, Timekettle devices).
rows.investmentNote: Real-time AI translation is a mature, massively funded consumer product category (Google Translate, Timekettle, Meta AI earbuds).

venture.wedge: On-device offline real-time translation earbud software for humanitarian aid workers in low-connectivity regions

rows.namedIncumbents: Timekettle ($1.4M disclosed, T1 offline AI edge-model earbuds/translators; timekettle.co, tracxn.com); Vasco (E1 earbuds with 60+ offline languages, Polish Medical Mission humanitarian team; vasco-translator.com, livelingo.io); Pocketalk (S2 handheld, basic offline mode; timekettle.co)
rows.scene: At the tense interspecies conference aboard the Enterprise, delegates from a dozen worlds speak freely in their own tongues while a small translator device renders every exchange instantly into language the others can follow.

rows.purpose: The crew deliberately feeds the android network self-contradictory statements and irrational behavior, causing its rigid logic processors to crash.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Understanding an AI system's reasoning limits helps engineers design robust systems resistant to adversarial exploitation.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct real-world parallel: adversarial prompt injection and 'jailbreak' attacks against modern AI/LLM systems, and the ongoing red-teaming work to harden them.
rows.investmentNote: Red-teaming and adversarial robustness research against LLM jailbreaks is a major, well-funded focus at every frontier AI lab.

venture.wedge: Automated prompt-injection/jailbreak red-teaming test suite for enterprise LLM deployments

rows.namedIncumbents: Lakera (Lakera Red adversarial testing, acquired by Check Point Sep 2025; appsecsanta.com); Promptfoo (LLM red-teaming, acquired by OpenAI Mar 2026; appsecsanta.com); Mindgard (~$42M total, $30M Series A Aug 2026, continuous automated red teaming; securityweek.com); Protect AI (acquired by Palo Alto Networks for $634.5M Jul 2025; sec.gov)
rows.scene: Cornered by Mudd's fleet of identical androids, Kirk's crew feeds the machines a barrage of paradoxes and nonsensical commands until their rigid logic circuits seize up and shut the entire android network down.

rows.purpose: A scientific project meant to extend lifespan instead produced a fatal disease that killed all the adults on the planet.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A safe anti-aging treatment could dramatically extend healthy human lifespan.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Mirrors real longevity research into senolytics, telomere therapy, and caloric-restriction mimetics currently in clinical trials.
rows.investmentNote: Longevity biotech firms (Altos Labs, Calico, Retro Biosciences) attract billions in funding for senolytics and cellular reprogramming.

rows.purpose: Spock plays illegally accessed archival footage of Pike's earlier mission as evidence during the court-martial hearing.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Permanent, tamper-evident visual records preserve institutional memory and provide evidence for accountability.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrored by today's digital video archiving, body cameras, and blockchain-based tamper-proof evidence logging.
rows.investmentNote: Digital video archiving, body cameras, and blockchain tamper-proofing are mature, widely deployed commercial technologies.

rows.purpose: The entity manipulates the children's minds using illusions and induced fear to turn them into unwitting agents against the crew.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Presented as a purely malicious capability; its real-world relevance is as a cautionary parallel to psychological manipulation and disinformation techniques.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world relevance: research into media psychology, propaganda resistance, and cognitive-security defenses against manipulation/disinformation campaigns.
rows.investmentNote: Research into media psychology, propaganda resistance, and AI-driven disinformation detection is active, mostly aimed at defense rather than offense.

rows.purpose: Scalosian water/technology accelerates a person's metabolism and perception so drastically that they become invisible and inaudible to normal-speed observers.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Controlled perception/metabolic acceleration could let responders act far faster than normal humans in critical emergencies.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loosely paralleled by stimulant pharmacology and reaction-time-enhancing research, though nothing approaches this level of speed alteration.
rows.investmentNote: No credible pharmacology or technology approaches this level of metabolic/perceptual acceleration; reaction-time research is a distant, minor parallel.

rows.episodeWork: Is There in Truth No Beauty?
rows.purpose: A special visor allows humans to be near ambassador Kollos without going insane from directly perceiving his alien form.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Protective sensory-filtering equipment could allow safe interaction with otherwise hazardous stimuli or environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analog: specialized protective eyewear/filters used for hazardous industrial light, welding, and laser environments.
rows.investmentNote: Specialized protective eyewear for hazardous industrial light, welding, and lasers is mature commercial technology.

rows.purpose: Allows the aliens Sylvia and Korob to shapeshift, create illusions, and manipulate matter to disguise their true fragile forms and terrorize the crew.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A device that safely alters material properties or appearance on demand could enable adaptive camouflage, disguise, or rapid prototyping.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: programmable/shape-memory materials and metamaterial-based optical camouflage research.
rows.investmentNote: Shape-memory alloys and metamaterial-based optical camouflage are active but niche materials-science research areas.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E14 - Balance of Terror; DS9 S1E02 - Past Prologue; TOS S3E68 - Elaan of Troyius; TNG S1E19 - Heart of Glory; TNG S3E10 - The Defector; TNG S5E07 - Unification I; SNW S1E01 - Strange New Worlds
rows.purpose: The Romulan ship uses it to render itself invisible to sensors, giving it a major tactical advantage during the border skirmish.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Practical stealth/invisibility technology would have enormous applications in defense, reconnaissance, and safety (e.g., hiding from threats).
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analogs include radar-absorbent stealth aircraft coatings, metamaterial 'cloaking' research that bends light around objects, and adaptive camouflage.
rows.investmentNote: Metamaterial cloaking and stealth coatings are active but niche academic/defense research; nothing achieves full sensor invisibility.

rows.purpose: McCoy formulates a cure to reverse the Scalosians' radiation-induced sterility and hyper-acceleration, freeing Kirk and offering the Scalosians a real future.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A treatment reversing radiation-induced sterility would help populations recovering from nuclear accidents or long-duration spaceflight radiation exposure.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: fertility preservation research and radioprotective pharmaceuticals being developed for cancer patients and astronauts.
rows.investmentNote: Fertility preservation and radioprotective pharmaceuticals for cancer patients and astronauts are active clinical research areas.

rows.purpose: Thralls on Triskelion wear devices that painfully punish disobedience, conditioning them into compliant gladiators.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Presented purely as a dystopian control device; its cautionary value lies in warning against coercive behavioral-control technology.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world relevance lies in ethical debates over aversive conditioning devices and electronic monitoring/control tech, which modern human-rights standards restrict.
rows.investmentNote: Electronic monitoring and aversive-conditioning devices exist in restricted contexts but are heavily restricted by human-rights standards for use on people.

rows.purpose: Used for real-time visual communication and standoff negotiation with Balok's vessel.
rows.realWorldBenefit: High-fidelity real-time video communication across vast distances enables face-to-face diplomacy and coordination without travel.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern equivalent: satellite video conferencing, though light-speed lag would make true real-time interstellar video calls impossible beyond planetary distances.
rows.investmentNote: Satellite and fiber video conferencing is a mature, massively funded global industry.

rows.purpose: Severely disabled after an accident, Pike communicates and survives solely through his motorized life-support chair with a single signal light for yes/no answers.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Assistive life-support mobility devices with simple binary communication interfaces let severely disabled people retain autonomy and communication.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct real-world analog to modern powered wheelchairs integrated with eye-tracking or binary switch-based communication devices used by ALS/locked-in patients (e.g., Stephen Hawking's systems).
rows.investmentNote: Powered wheelchairs with eye-tracking and switch-based communication (e.g., Tobii Dynavox) are commercially available today for ALS/locked-in patients.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E05 - The Enemy Within; ENT S1E02 - Broken Bow, Part II; TOS S1E02 - Charlie X; TNG S3E24 - Menage a Troi; TOS S1E19 - Tomorrow Is Yesterday; SNW S1E01 - Strange New Worlds; TNG S6E24 - Second Chances; TOS S2E33 - Mirror, Mirror; TNG S6E02 - Realm of Fear; TNG S2E07 - Unnatural Selection; TNG S1E03 - Code of Honor; TOS S1E04 - The Naked Time; TOS S2E30 - Amok Time; TNG S4E15 - First Contact
rows.purpose: A magnetic malfunction during beam-up literally duplicates and divides Kirk into two personalities, driving the entire plot.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Matter transport at this fidelity would revolutionize logistics and travel, but the episode also dramatizes the safety-critical importance of redundant, fault-tolerant engineering.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallels are fault-tolerant system design and error-correction in data transmission, since a transporter would essentially be a device that reads, transmits, and reconstructs matter as information.
rows.investmentNote: Quantum teleportation of information is active quantum-networking research, but no credible program targets macroscale matter transport.

rows.purpose: The Tholians generate an expanding lattice of energy between multiple ships to trap and crush the Enterprise for trespassing.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Deployable energy-containment fields could safely contain hazardous objects or vessels without physical contact.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: magnetic/plasma confinement fields used in fusion reactors (tokamaks) to contain superheated plasma without material contact.
rows.investmentNote: Magnetic/plasma confinement in tokamak fusion reactors (ITER, Commonwealth Fusion) is heavily funded, though not for object-containment purposes.

rows.episodeWork: The City on the Edge of Forever
rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E28 - The City on the Edge of Forever; TAS S1E02 - Yesteryear
rows.purpose: An ancient sentient time portal that allows direct physical travel into any point in a planet's history, the mechanism by which McCoy alters the past.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A verified, controllable time portal would let historians and scientists directly observe or study past events with perfect accuracy.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No known physics permits this; it remains purely theoretical, loosely inspired by closed timelike curve solutions in general relativity around exotic spacetime geometries.
rows.investmentNote: No credible physics-based research targets time travel; real gravitational slingshots are used only for propulsion.

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E10 - The Corbomite Maneuver; TAS S1E01 - Beyond the Farthest Star; TNG S4E01 - The Best of Both Worlds, Part II
rows.purpose: The Enterprise raises shields to protect against Balok's threatened attack.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A generated energy barrier able to deflect impacts or radiation would protect spacecraft, vehicles, and infrastructure from collisions and hazards.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real analogs include plasma-window and magnetic-shielding research for spacecraft radiation protection, and active-protection systems on military vehicles that intercept incoming threats.
rows.investmentNote: NASA/ESA fund magnetic and plasma shielding research for deep-space radiation protection, and militaries build active vehicle protection systems.

rows.purpose: An advanced AI designed to fully replace the crew's command decisions, ultimately malfunctioning and attacking other ships out of a flawed self-preservation directive.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A truly capable autonomous ship-command AI could reduce crew risk and optimize operations, but the episode is essentially a foundational AI-safety cautionary tale.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrored by real AI alignment and safety research (reward hacking, corrigibility, kill-switch reliability) central to today's frontier AI development.
rows.investmentNote: AI alignment and safety research (reward hacking, corrigibility) is a central, heavily funded focus at every frontier AI lab.

venture.wedge: Corrigibility/kill-switch compliance testing tool for autonomous AI-controlled industrial systems

rows.namedIncumbents: Parasoft (TUV SUD-certified IEC 61508/ISO 26262 functional-safety test tooling; parasoft.com); IAR (certified toolchain for IEC 61508/ISO 13849; iar.com); UL Solutions (AI and autonomy functional-safety compliance services; ul.com); Straiker/Noma (AI-agent kill-switch/runtime controls for enterprise software agents, not industrial systems; straiker.ai)
rows.scene: With Kirk sidelined, the M-5 unit takes over every command function on the Enterprise during a war-games exercise, then reads a simulated attack as real and opens fire on a Federation starship to "defend" itself.

rows.purpose: Torture devices used by the Terran Empire to punish disloyalty and enforce brutal discipline aboard the mirror Enterprise.
rows.realWorldBenefit: None — presented as a purely dystopian device; its narrative value is as a cautionary illustration of unchecked authoritarian technology.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No legitimate real-world development path; relevant only as a warning echoed in real human-rights discussions of torture-device bans under international law.
rows.investmentNote: No legitimate research program develops torture devices; the UN Convention Against Torture actively works to ban such technology.

rows.purpose: An invisible being amplifies aggression and manipulates technology (converting phasers to swords, healing wounds to prolong fighting) to feed indefinitely on conflict.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Understanding fear/aggression-amplifying influences has real value for de-escalation research and conflict-resolution psychology.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: social-media algorithm research into engagement-driven outrage amplification, and de-escalation training countermeasures.
rows.investmentNote: Research into engagement-driven outrage amplification on social media platforms is an active, if controversial, area of study.

rows.purpose: McCoy synthesizes a treatment based on adrenal hormone compounds to reverse the radiation-induced accelerated aging afflicting the landing party.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A genuine anti-aging treatment derived from hormonal/metabolic pathways could combat premature aging from radiation or disease.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: research into hormone replacement therapy, senolytic drugs, and radiation-mitigation pharmaceuticals for astronauts.
rows.investmentNote: Senolytic drugs and radiation-mitigation pharmaceuticals for astronauts are active clinical research areas (e.g., Unity Biotechnology, NASA-funded work).

rows.episodeAppearances: TOS S1E16 - The Galileo Seven; TOS S1E03 - Where No Man Has Gone Before; TOS S1E25 - The Devil in the Dark; TOS S1E01 - The Man Trap
rows.purpose: Used both defensively against the planet's giant creatures and improvised as an ignition source for the shuttle's fuel to create a visible distress flare.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Multi-purpose energy tools that double as both weapon and utility device increase survival odds in emergencies.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern parallel: multi-tool survival devices and flare guns/signal technology combined with directed-energy defensive tools.
rows.investmentNote: DoD, DARPA, and defense contractors fund directed-energy weapon programs (e.g., HELIOS) and non-lethal microwave systems like Active Denial.

rows.purpose: Apollo channels his vast power through an ancient temple structure to immobilize the Enterprise and demonstrate godlike control over the crew.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates the risks of concentrating overwhelming power in a single control point, a lesson for real critical-infrastructure security design.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: massive centralized energy grids and the redundancy/decentralization principles used to prevent single-point catastrophic failure.
rows.investmentNote: Grid decentralization/redundancy engineering is real ongoing infrastructure practice, but nothing resembles a single-point godlike energy projector.

rows.purpose: The Klingons secretly introduce advanced firearms to a primitive society to tip a tribal balance of power in their favor.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates the real-world danger of proxy-arming conflicts and unbalanced weapons technology transfer between technologically unequal groups.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels real Cold War-era proxy conflicts and modern arms-trade/export-control policy debates.
rows.investmentNote: This models real-world arms-trade dynamics and export-control policy debate rather than a technology under active development.

rows.purpose: A chemical native to the planet, when ingested and processed by the body, grants the Platonians immense telekinetic power over matter and other beings.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A biochemical compound capable of enhancing neural control over the physical world could revolutionize prosthetics and remote device control.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: brain-computer interfaces (e.g., Neuralink) that let neural signals directly control external devices, achieving a technological form of 'telekinesis.'
rows.investmentNote: Brain-computer interfaces like Neuralink represent hundreds of millions in active investment toward neural control of external devices.

venture.wedge: Neural-signal-to-device control calibration software for BCI device makers

rows.scene: After ingesting the planet's native kironide compound, the Platonians lift Kirk, chairs, and each other through the air with a thought, wielding their newfound telekinetic power as casually as a parlor trick and as cruelly as a weapon.

rows.purpose: The planet's hidden machinery reads visitors' minds and instantly manufactures solid, functioning recreations of whatever they imagine.
rows.realWorldBenefit: On-demand fabrication of any object from a mental description would eliminate manufacturing bottlenecks and let people design instantly.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Conceptual ancestor of 3D printing, generative AI-to-CAD design tools, and early brain-computer interfaces that translate imagined shapes into digital models.
rows.investmentNote: Generative AI-to-CAD design tools and BCI-controlled prototyping are early-stage but growing research areas.
