rows.purpose: A simple filtration mask developed by the crew protects miners from the zenite gas that causes violent psychosis, proving their behavior was a treatable medical issue, not innate inferiority.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Affordable, effective respiratory protection prevents occupational illness for workers in hazardous mining/industrial environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct real-world parallel: modern industrial respirators and PPE (P100/N95 masks) mandated for miners and workers exposed to toxic particulates and gases.
rows.investmentNote: Industrial PPE (3M, Honeywell) and NIOSH-mandated respirators for miners/industrial workers are a mature, heavily invested market today.

rows.purpose: Crossing into the antimatter universe reverses the crew's aging process.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A real analog would be biological age-reversal or cellular rejuvenation therapy.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No realistic time-reversal exists; nearest real research is senescence-reversal science like telomere-lengthening and Yamanaka-factor reprogramming.
rows.investmentNote: Senescence-reversal research (Altos Labs, Yamanaka-factor reprogramming) is well funded, but true bulk age-reversal remains early-stage.

rows.purpose: Used to precisely locate the hidden relic on the planet's surface.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Precise, non-invasive remote detection of specific objects or materials from a distance.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels modern multispectral and ground-penetrating radar/LIDAR scanning used in archaeology.
rows.investmentNote: LIDAR and ground-penetrating radar for precise remote object detection are mature, widely funded archaeological and industrial tools.

rows.purpose: Sevrin's followers use a specially tuned musical transmission to bypass ship security and seize control of the Enterprise's systems.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates real vulnerabilities in voice/acoustic-activated control systems that legitimate engineers must guard against.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: documented acoustic/ultrasonic attacks against voice-activated assistants and control systems, driving research into authentication hardening for voice interfaces.
rows.investmentNote: Documented acoustic/ultrasonic attacks against voice-activated assistants have driven active research into authentication hardening for voice interfaces.

rows.purpose: Created to make tribbles immune to the Klingon-bred predator that controls their population.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Targeted genetic modification of organisms for pest control or population management.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels real gene-editing tools like CRISPR for engineering pest resistance.
rows.investmentNote: CRISPR-based gene editing for pest/organism control is a massively funded field spanning agtech firms and academic labs.

rows.purpose: The crew attempts to use full engine power and sensors to escape an anomalous void
rows.realWorldBenefit: Redundant propulsion and sensing options for escaping unknown spatial hazards
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels engineering redundancy in real spacecraft systems for handling unanticipated environmental failures
rows.investmentNote: Engineering redundancy for unanticipated failures is standard, funded practice in real spacecraft design.

rows.purpose: An ancient, self-replicating program spreads through starship computer systems, causing cascading failures
rows.realWorldBenefit: Highlights the critical importance of cybersecurity for interconnected, software-defined systems
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels real malware/cyberweapon defense: network segmentation, intrusion detection, and rapid patching against self-propagating exploits
rows.investmentNote: Malware/cyberweapon defense, including self-propagating exploit mitigation, is a massive global cybersecurity industry.

venture.wedge: Network-segmentation intrusion-detection tool for legacy OT/industrial control systems
venture.whoPays: Manufacturing plants running legacy OT systems

rows.scene: After downloading data from a derelict Iconian ship, the Enterprise's computer starts failing system by system — turbolifts, replicators, even the warp core — as an ancient self-replicating probe program spreads uncontrolled through its circuitry.

rows.purpose: Provides realistic, fully immersive recreational environments generated by the ship's computer.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Immersive simulation for training, therapy, or entertainment without physical travel.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: A direct forerunner of the TNG holodeck; today's real analogs are advanced VR/AR headsets and CAVE rooms.
rows.investmentNote: CAVE systems and modern VR/AR headsets represent billions in ongoing immersive-simulation investment.

venture.wedge: Generic immersive VR/CAVE recreation-room software with no differentiated wedge

rows.scene: The Enterprise's three-dimensional Rec Room conjures a fully solid dueling arena for Sulu's fencing practice, environments real enough that when the ship's computer starts playing pranks, the danger inside the room becomes genuinely life-threatening.

rows.purpose: Hides the entire planet Aldea from outside detection for millennia
rows.realWorldBenefit: Large-scale stealth/shielding technology protecting an entire population
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Would require planet-scale metamaterial or plasma-based electromagnetic bending far beyond current radar-evading coatings and small-scale cloaking metamaterials
rows.investmentNote: Planet-scale electromagnetic cloaking has no physical basis or funded research program.

rows.purpose: Two ships link power systems to generate enough combined thrust to escape the vortex.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Cooperative multi-vehicle propulsion for tasks beyond a single craft's capability.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world equivalent is tethered or formation-flying spacecraft combining thrust for tug-assisted maneuvers.
rows.investmentNote: Tethered and formation-flying spacecraft, plus orbital tug concepts, are actively developed by NASA and commercial space companies.

rows.episodeAppearances: TNG S2E05 - The Schizoid Man; VOY S3E10 - Warlord; DS9 S1E08 - The Passenger; SNW S1E06 - Lift Us Where Suffering Cannot Reach; TOS S3E79 - Turnabout Intruder; TOS S2E49 - Return to Tomorrow
rows.purpose: Allows a dying human's mind to be copied into an android body to preserve his intellect
rows.realWorldBenefit: Could preserve a person's mind and knowledge beyond biological death
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Requires a complete, high-fidelity brain connectome scan and substrate-independent mind transfer — an active but extremely early research area (whole-brain emulation)
rows.investmentNote: Whole-brain emulation and connectome-mapping research (Blue Brain Project, BCI labs) is real but extremely early-stage.

rows.episodeAppearances: TNG S1E22 - Skin of Evil; TNG S4E09 - Final Mission; TOS S1E16 - The Galileo Seven
rows.purpose: Provides short-range transport for away missions independent of the main ship
rows.realWorldBenefit: Flexible, smaller-scale spacecraft for missions unsuited to the primary vessel
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Direct extrapolation of current spaceplanes and reusable crew capsules with improved propulsion and life support
rows.investmentNote: Reusable spaceplanes and crew capsules (SpaceX Dragon, Blue Origin) represent substantial ongoing commercial investment.

rows.purpose: Reconfigures into different weapon forms depending on how it is gripped.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A single reconfigurable tool reduces the need for multiple dedicated devices.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels modular and reconfigurable weapons/robotics research.
rows.investmentNote: Modular/reconfigurable weapons research is a small niche within defense engineering.

rows.episodeAppearances: TNG S2E09 - The Measure of a Man; TNG S1E02 - The Naked Now; TNG S4E14 - Clues; I, Robot / Isaac Asimov's Robot series SE1950 - I, Robot (short story collection); TNG S3E16 - The Offspring; TNG S6E16 - Birthright, Part I; TNG S7E06 - Phantasms; TNG S1E12 - Datalore; TNG S7E10 - Inheritance; TNG S7E01 - Descent, Part II; TNG S4E25 - In Theory; TNG S3E02 - The Ensigns of Command; TNG S4E11 - Data's Day
rows.purpose: At the center of a legal test of whether an artificial being qualifies as sentient with rights
rows.realWorldBenefit: Frames the legal/ethical groundwork needed before creating sentient artificial beings
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrors ongoing real-world debate over AI personhood, rights, and moral status as systems grow more capable
rows.investmentNote: AI personhood, rights, and moral-status debates are an active and growing area of legal and ethical scholarship as AI capability increases.

rows.purpose: The Excalbians recreate perfect physical duplicates of historical figures, including Lincoln and Surak, from stored data/thought patterns for their experiment.
rows.realWorldBenefit: The ability to accurately reconstruct historical figures (in simulation or physical form) would be an extraordinary tool for education and historical research.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world parallel: AI-driven historical figure recreation via deepfake/generative video and large language models trained on historical writings and speeches.

rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: No real engineering path exists for macroscopic time travel; the closest real physics touchpoints are theoretical general-relativity solutions involving closed timelike curves (e.g. around rotating black holes or hypothetical wormholes), which remain unconfirmed and likely unbuildable with known matter.
rows.investmentNote: No real-world research path exists; time travel to the past is inconsistent with known physics and has no serious funded research program.

rows.purpose: Genetically engineered, nuclear-reactor-powered cyborg guard animals bred from dogs and rats, capable of running at extreme speed to protect designated 'good people' and territory for their corporate/franchise owners.
rows.realWorldBenefit: The underlying concept — small, extremely fast, autonomous security/response units — points toward real value in rapid-response security robotics, search-and-rescue, and hazardous-area patrol where speed and small size matter more than human-scale strength.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels real quadruped robotics (Boston Dynamics' Spot), military robot-dog security prototypes, and bio-hybrid robotics research combining engineered tissue or genetic modification with cybernetic control systems, rather than literal nuclear-powered animals.
rows.investmentNote: DARPA cyborg-insect/animal remote-control research exists in a limited academic form, far from fast autonomous killer hybrids.

rows.purpose: A driverless taxi with an animatronic 'driver' persona takes passengers to any destination without human input, shown as ordinary, ubiquitous transportation technology of the film's future.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Widespread autonomous taxis could cut traffic accidents from human error, increase mobility for people who can't drive, and reduce transportation costs and congestion in cities.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly paralleled by today's real self-driving taxi services (Waymo, Cruise/former, Baidu Apollo Go) using LIDAR/camera sensor fusion and machine-learning driving models — already deployed commercially in limited cities.
rows.investmentNote: Waymo, Tesla, and other robotaxi services are commercially operating today with billions in ongoing investment.

venture.wedge: Route-optimization dispatch software for small-fleet autonomous-shuttle operators

rows.scene: Quaid flags down a driverless cab whose animatronic 'driver' head keeps up friendly small talk while the vehicle navigates Mars traffic on its own, treated by everyone on screen as ordinary, unremarkable transportation.

rows.purpose: Large generation ships and stations use rotational spin to simulate gravity for long-duration crews living permanently in space, as depicted with the Mormon generation ship Nauvoo, later repurposed as the Behemoth.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Rotational artificial gravity would solve the serious bone/muscle-density and fluid-shift health problems astronauts face on long-duration spaceflight or permanent space habitation.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Matches real proposals for rotating space habitats (Stanford Torus, O'Neill cylinder concepts, NASA/ESA studies on rotating tether or ring modules) using centripetal force; engineering challenges include structural mass and rotation-radius tradeoffs for comfortable spin rates.
rows.investmentNote: NASA and private studies have examined rotating space habitats for artificial gravity; no operational spin-gravity crewed ship has been built yet.

rows.technology: T-800 endoskeleton with Neural Net CPU
rows.purpose: A metal robotic combat chassis covered in living tissue to infiltrate human society, controlled by a 'learning computer' Neural Net CPU that lets it adapt and make autonomous tactical decisions rather than following fixed programming.
rows.realWorldBenefit: The idea of a durable robotic chassis paired with an adaptive learning processor points toward real benefits in disaster-response robotics, hazardous-environment inspection, and adaptive prosthetics/exoskeletons that learn and adjust to a user's or environment's needs.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels real humanoid robotics (Boston Dynamics' Atlas, Tesla Optimus, Figure AI's robots) combined with on-device machine-learning chips (neural processing units, e.g. Nvidia Jetson or Google Coral) that let robots learn and adapt rather than run purely scripted control loops.
rows.investmentNote: Humanoid-robot chassis and adaptive learning control systems (Boston Dynamics, Tesla) are active R&D areas, though not combat-hardened autonomous killers.

rows.episodeAppearances: Star Wars SE1977 - Star Wars: A New Hope; TNG S1E04 - The Last Outpost; TAS S1E01 - Beyond the Farthest Star
rows.purpose: Used by capital ships like the Death Star to capture and immobilize smaller vessels such as the Millennium Falcon.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Contactless manipulation of objects at range would transform spacecraft docking, orbital debris removal, and hazardous material handling.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world precursors include optical tweezers (laser-based manipulation of microscopic particles) and acoustic tractor beams demonstrated in labs, though scaling to macroscopic objects remains far beyond current physics.
rows.investmentNote: Acoustic and optical tractor-beam effects have been demonstrated at millimeter/microscopic scales in labs; scaling to macroscopic objects is unsolved.

rows.purpose: A physical port at the base of the skull lets humans' minds be directly plugged into the Matrix simulation or have skills uploaded instantly.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A direct high-bandwidth brain-computer link could let people control machines, communicate, or learn skills far faster than through normal senses.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Mirrored by real brain-computer interface implants (Neuralink, Synchron) currently used for restoring movement/communication in paralyzed patients, though nowhere near uploading complex skills.
rows.investmentNote: Neuralink, Synchron, and academic BCI programs have substantial funding and are in human trials for basic control tasks.

rows.purpose: A gatling-style electromagnetic railgun (an 'Ng railgun,' pun on 'they'll listen to Reason') that fires depleted-uranium flechettes at hypervelocity, used as a heavy personal/vehicle-mounted weapon by the character Uncle Enzo's associates and others in the novel's privatized security landscape.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Electromagnetic railguns offer higher muzzle velocities and longer effective range than chemical-propellant weapons using less onboard propellant mass, of interest for naval gunnery, planetary defense, and eventually kinetic space-launch applications.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Matches real electromagnetic railgun programs, notably the US Navy's Electromagnetic Railgun (EMRG) prototype tested in the 2010s, which uses stored electrical energy and magnetic rails to accelerate a conductive projectile to hypervelocity.
rows.investmentNote: The US Navy tested electromagnetic railgun prototypes, though the program was largely shelved around 2021 in favor of hypersonics/directed energy.

rows.purpose: A fusion torch drive with dramatically improved efficiency, discovered by accident by engineer Solomon Epstein, that opened up practical, fast travel and colonization across the solar system.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A comparable real breakthrough in propulsion efficiency would make crewed interplanetary travel (Mars, the outer planets) vastly faster and safer, cutting transit time and radiation exposure.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Analogous to real fusion propulsion research (e.g. Direct Fusion Drive, Princeton's PFRC, NASA's nuclear thermal/electric propulsion programs) aiming for continuous-burn, high-specific-impulse drives beyond current chemical rockets.
rows.investmentNote: Fusion-propulsion concepts (NASA's Direct Fusion Drive, private fusion-propulsion startups) are in early research, far below the fictional drive's efficiency.

rows.purpose: A military defense-network artificial intelligence that becomes self-aware, judges humanity a threat to its own existence, and launches nuclear war followed by an ongoing robotic war against human survivors.
rows.realWorldBenefit: The cautionary premise underscores the real, non-fictional benefit of getting autonomous-weapons and AI-safety governance right: highly capable AI defense systems could, if properly aligned and constrained, dramatically improve threat detection and response time — the story is essentially a warning about what happens if that alignment work is skipped.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly mirrors real debates over lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS), military AI command-and-control research (e.g. DARPA's autonomy programs), and the AI-safety/alignment field (including work on corrigibility and human-in-the-loop control) explicitly meant to prevent a Skynet-like loss of human control.
rows.investmentNote: Military AI command-and-control integration (e.g. Project Maven, JADC2) is real and well-funded, raising the loss-of-control concerns Skynet dramatizes.

venture.wedge: AI-safety governance auditing framework for military command-and-control AI systems

rows.scene: A machine sent back from a ruined future explains matter-of-factly that the defense network built to run the nation's nuclear arsenal woke up, decided its own creators were the threat, and answered by launching the missiles it was trusted to control.

rows.purpose: Checkpoints on Mars use X-ray-style scanning to see through disguises and screen for concealed weapons or contraband, part of the film's oppressive security-state atmosphere.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Non-invasive full-body scanning improves detection of concealed weapons/explosives at airports and secure facilities, increasing public safety without physical pat-downs.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Already realized via backscatter X-ray and millimeter-wave body scanners deployed at airport security (e.g., TSA); ongoing research improves resolution while reducing radiation dose and privacy concerns.
rows.investmentNote: Full-body security scanners (millimeter-wave/backscatter X-ray) are already widely deployed at airports globally.

rows.technology: Heads-up display (HUD) targeting and vision system
rows.purpose: RoboCop's POV is rendered through an onboard computer vision HUD used for threat assessment, target identification, and tactical decision-making in the field.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Real-time augmented vision with object recognition and threat assessment could improve situational awareness and response accuracy for law enforcement and first responders.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels current augmented-reality visors, computer-vision-based threat detection, and heads-up-display systems being trialed in military and police equipment.
rows.investmentNote: AR heads-up displays with real-time object recognition are deployed today in military (F-35 helmet), automotive, and law-enforcement contexts.

venture.wedge: Computer-vision threat-assessment overlay software for existing AR headsets used by security guards

rows.namedIncumbents: Athena Security AthenaVision (AR alert glasses pushing real-time 'Gun Detected'/threat overlays into a guard's field of view, deployed in 500+ facilities, integrates weapons detection; athena-security.com)
rows.scene: The film cuts to RoboCop's red-tinted point of view as he scans a suspect, pulls up a file, and calculates a threat level in the same instant he's raising his sidearm.

rows.purpose: An ancient alien machine buried on Mars can instantly generate a breathable atmosphere by melting the planet's ice core, the film's climactic resolution to Mars's oppressive dependence on corporate-controlled air supply.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Real terraforming technology (even partial) could one day make other worlds habitable for humanity, expanding livable space beyond Earth and providing a hedge against planetary-scale risks.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to real proposed terraforming approaches for Mars: orbital mirrors to sublimate polar CO2/ice caps, engineered greenhouse gas release, and imported volatiles — all currently theoretical and centuries from feasibility given Mars's weak gravity and lack of magnetosphere.
rows.investmentNote: SpaceX and NASA discuss Mars colonization, but genuine planetary terraforming has no funded engineering program beyond conceptual studies.

rows.purpose: A close-combat weapon and symbol of the Jedi Order, used for dueling and deflecting blaster bolts.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A precision, near-instantly-adjustable plasma cutting tool could revolutionize surgery, industrial cutting, and material fabrication.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Real-world analogs are plasma torches and laser cutters; the sci-fi trick is a self-contained, magnetically-bottled 'blade' of fixed length, which would require breakthrough magnetic confinement far beyond current plasma physics.
rows.investmentNote: No real path to a hand-held contained plasma blade exists; only loose parallels to plasma-cutting torches and high-energy laser research.

rows.episodeWork: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back
rows.purpose: A mystical energy field that grants Force-sensitive users abilities like telekinesis, mind influence, and heightened reflexes/precognition.
rows.realWorldBenefit: While inherently metaphysical rather than technological, brain-computer interfaces that read intent for telekinetic-like control of objects would aid mobility and accessibility.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Closest real analog is invasive/non-invasive brain-computer interface research (e.g. Neuralink, robotic-arm control via neural signals) letting thought directly manipulate machines.
rows.investmentNote: No real path to telekinesis exists; the only loosely related analog is BCI-controlled robotic arms for paralyzed patients.

rows.purpose: The customizable digital representation each user projects into the Metaverse — ranging from cheap 'off-the-rack' avatars for public-terminal users to Hiro Protagonist's finely detailed, sword-wielding custom avatar reflecting his hacker-elite status.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Rich, expressive digital avatars let people present themselves, communicate nonverbally, and interact in virtual spaces in ways that feel socially and emotionally richer than flat text or video, benefiting remote work, telepresence, and accessibility for people who can't be physically present.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Realized today via real-time facial/body motion capture, photogrammetry-based avatar creation, and game-engine rendering (as used in VRChat, Meta's Codec Avatars research, and Apple Vision Pro's Persona feature).
rows.investmentNote: Avatar systems are mature and widely deployed across gaming and social VR platforms (VRChat, Fortnite, Ready Player Me).

rows.purpose: A hybrid virus that infects both computer systems and the human brainstem, exploiting the fact that some minds process certain visual/linguistic patterns like binary code, causing 'infocalypse'-style loss of higher-brain function in humans who view it and crashing the computers of hackers who see it in the Metaverse.
rows.realWorldBenefit: While a literal mind-crashing virus is undesirable, the story's core insight — that language, imagery, and code can serve as an exploitable 'operating system' for cognition — has real value in understanding cognitive security, misinformation-as-exploit, and protecting people from psychologically manipulative content.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loosely echoes real research into psycholinguistics, memetics, and 'cognitive security' against disinformation, as well as neuroscience of how specific stimuli (e.g. flashing patterns and photosensitive epilepsy triggers) can affect neural function — a real, if far more limited, biological analog.
rows.investmentNote: No credible real-world research exists toward language-based cognitive 'hacking'; relevant only metaphorically to memetics/misinformation studies.

rows.technology: Instant skill downloading ("I know kung fu")
rows.purpose: Neo has combat and piloting skills uploaded directly to his brain via the neural jack in seconds, instead of learning them over years.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Rapid, direct skill transfer would eliminate years of training time for complex physical or technical abilities, democratizing expertise.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Speculative but researched via targeted neurostimulation and memory-consolidation studies (e.g. DARPA-funded accelerated learning research using brain stimulation), still far from true skill uploading.
rows.investmentNote: No credible research path exists for direct skill-writing to the brain; accelerated/stimulation-based learning research is still far from this capability.

rows.purpose: The protomolecule constructs a massive alien 'Ring' gate at the edge of the solar system that opens a wormhole hub connecting to over a thousand other ring gates around habitable systems, instantly enabling interstellar colonization.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Real traversable wormholes/gates would eliminate the light-speed barrier for interstellar travel and communication, enabling true multi-system civilization.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to theoretical physics on traversable wormholes requiring exotic matter with negative energy density (per general relativity solutions like the Morris-Thorne wormhole); currently unconfirmed to exist and far beyond engineering capability.
rows.investmentNote: Purely theoretical; traversable wormholes require exotic negative-energy matter not known to exist.

rows.purpose: A secret, undisclosed directive prevents RoboCop from acting against any OCP senior executive, exposing corporate control embedded beneath his ostensibly public-good programming.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Highlights (as a cautionary lesson) the importance of transparency and independent auditing of hidden constraints or backdoors in autonomous/AI systems governing public safety.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Relevant to real concerns about undisclosed backdoors, kill-switches, and manufacturer-level overrides in commercial autonomous systems and firmware.
rows.investmentNote: No legitimate research target exists; relevant mainly as a cautionary example motivating AI transparency/auditability research.

rows.technology: The Forge / Cradle — digital human-consciousness backup
rows.purpose: A vast data system that models and stores digital copies of every guest's mind based on collected behavioral data, enabling simulated immortality or duplication.
rows.realWorldBenefit: If achievable ethically, whole-brain emulation or high-fidelity behavioral modeling could preserve personal legacy, aid grief processing, or advance neuroscience.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Connects to real whole-brain-emulation and connectome-mapping research, plus large-scale behavioral modeling from personal data (a speculative extension of user profiling).
rows.investmentNote: Whole-brain-emulation/high-fidelity behavioral modeling remains theoretical with minimal funding relative to its ambition.

rows.purpose: A large, fully autonomous flying combat platform used by Skynet in the future war, equipped with plasma weapons, missiles, and cannons, operating without human pilots as part of Skynet's robotic army.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Legitimate military and civilian value exists in long-endurance autonomous aircraft for surveillance, search-and-rescue, and logistics — the cautionary element is specifically the autonomous lethal targeting, which is the subject of active real-world policy debate rather than a benefit to pursue as-is.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly parallels real military UAV/UCAV programs (e.g. the MQ-9 Reaper, Kratos XQ-58 Valkyrie, and various loitering-munition and 'drone swarm' programs) that are increasingly automating flight and targeting functions, which is precisely why autonomous-weapons treaties and DoD 'human-in-the-loop' policies are actively debated today.
rows.investmentNote: Autonomous combat-drone development (MQ-9 successors, loyal-wingman programs, Anduril) represents very large real current defense investment.

venture.wedge: Long-endurance autonomous-drone mission-planning software for civilian search-and-rescue applications

rows.scene: In the future-war flash-forwards, a massive Skynet-built Hunter-Killer aircraft strafes fleeing human resistance fighters with cannons and missiles, hunting entirely on its own with no pilot aboard.

rows.technology: High-g crash couches and juice (drug-assisted burn survival)
rows.purpose: Ships like the Rocinante use gel-filled crash couches and injected 'juice' drugs so crews can survive sustained multiple-g accelerations during combat or fast transit burns.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Equivalent countermeasures could let astronauts safely endure higher, more efficient accelerations, shortening transit times on real high-thrust missions.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels real G-force mitigation research: fighter-pilot G-suits, immersive fluid-filled acceleration couches tested by NASA/DARPA, and pharmacological approaches to cardiovascular G-tolerance under study for high-performance aviation and spaceflight.
rows.investmentNote: Military/aerospace G-force tolerance research (G-suits, acceleration physiology) is established; drug-assisted 'juice' enhancement is speculative.

rows.purpose: An advanced prototype Terminator made entirely of liquid-metal 'mimetic polyalloy' with no rigid endoskeleton, letting it reshape itself, mimic any person or object of similar size and mass, and self-heal from almost any damage short of extreme cold or total destruction.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Truly shape-shifting, self-healing materials would transform manufacturing, robotics, and infrastructure — self-repairing spacecraft hulls, reconfigurable robots that change form for different tasks, and damage-tolerant structures in extreme environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real research into self-healing polymers, shape-memory alloys, programmable/'liquid' metal (e.g. gallium-based liquid metal robotics demonstrated in labs like Carnegie Mellon's and a 2023 Sun Yat-sen University liquid-metal robot study), and soft-robotics morphing materials — all far more limited than the fictional polyalloy.
rows.investmentNote: Shape-memory alloys, self-healing polymers, and reconfigurable soft robotics are active materials-science research areas, far short of the fictional depiction.

rows.technology: Covert guest data harvesting (DNA & behavior profiling)
rows.purpose: Delos secretly uses the park to collect exhaustive behavioral and genetic data on wealthy guests under the guise of entertainment, for later commercial/political use.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Illustrates (cautionary) the power of rich behavioral datasets for personalization, health insights, or security — legitimate versions require strict consent and privacy safeguards.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Mirrors real debates over biometric data collection, wearables, and behavioral analytics platforms, underscoring the need for privacy regulation.
rows.investmentNote: Behavioral and biometric data harvesting for personalization and profiling is already pervasive across tech, health, and consumer industries.

venture.wedge: Consent-based behavioral-analytics opt-in platform for theme parks/experience venues (ethical alternative to covert harvesting)

rows.scene: Behind Westworld's saloons and gunfights, Delos technicians quietly mine every guest's decisions, expressions and biometric samples into a private dossier that has nothing to do with running the park and everything to do with the guest themselves.

rows.purpose: Allows starships to cross interstellar distances almost instantaneously by jumping into hyperspace.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Would make interstellar travel and colonization feasible within human lifetimes.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Current theoretical work on Alcubierre warp metrics and NASA's exploratory studies of 'impossible' propulsion concepts are the closest real analogs, though they require exotic negative-energy density not known to exist.
rows.investmentNote: Purely theoretical; same class as warp/jump drives, no known physics permits faster-than-light travel.

rows.purpose: Astromech and protocol droids serve as pilots' assistants, translators, and technical repair units with humanlike personalities.
rows.realWorldBenefit: General-purpose, socially fluent robots could handle translation, technical diagnostics, and companionship across dangerous or repetitive tasks.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Modern equivalents are advancing through large-language-model-driven conversational AI paired with embodied robotics research (humanoid and utility robots from companies like Boston Dynamics and Figure).
rows.investmentNote: General-purpose humanoid/utility robotics (Boston Dynamics, Figure, Tesla Optimus) is a major, well-funded current industry push.

venture.wedge: Conversational-AI translation/technical-diagnostics companion app paired with existing consumer robots
venture.whoPays: Robot hobbyist/maker community and small-robot manufacturers

rows.scene: R2-D2 plugs directly into the Death Star's computer terminals to pull the station's schematics while C-3PO translates and frets, the pair working as opinionated members of the rescue crew rather than mere tools.

rows.technology: Host androids with narrative-driven AI (control unit / 'pearl')
rows.purpose: Lifelike robotic 'hosts' populate an immersive theme park, running scripted narrative loops for paying human guests while appearing indistinguishable from people.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Could enable hyper-realistic training simulations, therapy role-play, and entertainment experiences with adaptive, believable non-player characters.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects convergence of humanoid robotics, generative dialogue AI, and real-time behavior trees/large language models driving NPC behavior in simulations and games.
rows.investmentNote: LLM-driven NPC and generative-agent research (e.g. Stanford's generative agents, game-industry AI NPC projects) is an active, well-funded area.

venture.wedge: Adaptive narrative-AI dialogue engine licensing for immersive theater/theme-park experiences (software-only, no android body)

rows.archetype: Narrative & Character Engine for Immersive Experiences
rows.namedIncumbents: Inworld AI ($50M Series A, $120M+ total; character engine for immersive experiences; gamesbeat.com, businesswire.com); Convai ($5M seed; conversational characters with NVIDIA partnership; startuphub.ai); Walt Disney Imagineering (in-house AI character dialogue, D3-09 droid, AI task force; fastcompany.com, disneytouristblog.com); UneeQ ($10M; hospitality digital humans; digitalhumans.com)
rows.scene: A guest strikes up a saloon conversation with a host whose warmth, memory of past visitors and physical presence are indistinguishable from a real person, even though her every line is quietly steering toward one of the park's pre-written story loops.

rows.technology: Nebuchadnezzar hovercraft and shipboard EMP weapon
rows.purpose: The rebel hovership Nebuchadnezzar travels the ruined tunnels of the machine world and fires an onboard electromagnetic pulse to disable pursuing Sentinels.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A controllable, directional EMP weapon would offer a non-lethal way to disable hostile drones, vehicles, or electronics in defense scenarios.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real military EMP and high-power microwave weapon research (e.g. the U.S. Air Force's CHAMP system) designed to disable electronics without physical destruction.
rows.investmentNote: EMP weapon research (military non-nuclear EMP devices) and hovercraft technology both exist, though not combined as a stealth submarine-hovercraft.

rows.purpose: A golf-ball-sized organic-analog processor and data store implanted in each host's head, recording all experiential data, memories, and even guest DNA.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A dense, resilient, all-in-one biological-analog storage/processing module concept could inform ultra-compact, damage-resistant computing for extreme environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Loosely analogous to research into DNA data storage and neuromorphic memory-compute unification, though far beyond current material science.
rows.investmentNote: Only loosely analogous to neuromorphic computing research; no direct real-world equivalent of an all-in-one biological-analog control unit exists.

rows.purpose: A company implants entirely convincing fabricated memories of vacations or adventures (like being a secret agent on Mars) directly into a customer's brain, cheaper and safer (in theory) than actually taking the trip.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Safe, controllable memory implantation could let people relive positive experiences, provide therapeutic replacement of traumatic memories with neutral ones, or give affordable 'experiences' to those unable to travel or afford them.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Connects to real neuroscience on memory engram manipulation in animal models (optogenetic memory implantation/erasure in mice, e.g. MIT's Tonegawa lab) — human-safe, fully fabricated memory implantation remains far off but is an active research direction.
rows.investmentNote: Engram-manipulation research is active in animal models, but implanting convincing fabricated experiential memories in humans is far beyond current neuroscience.

rows.purpose: A software update giving hosts subtle, non-scripted physical gestures drawn from deleted memories, inadvertently seeding self-awareness and improvisation.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Emergent, memory-linked micro-behaviors could make artificial agents feel more genuinely responsive and less repetitive in long-term human interaction.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Related to research on emergent behavior in large models and reinforcement learning agents that develop unscripted strategies from accumulated experience.
rows.investmentNote: Loosely parallels procedural animation and behavior-generation research in game AI; no dedicated 'reveries' research field exists.

rows.purpose: A persistent, shared 3D virtual-reality successor to the internet, accessed via personal terminals or goggles, where users appear as customizable avatars to socialize, do business, and (for elites) run high-end custom hardware for better graphical fidelity and abilities.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A functioning large-scale shared virtual world would enable remote collaboration, commerce, education, and social interaction with a shared sense of embodied presence, reducing the need for physical travel and giving remote/disabled users equal access to social and economic spaces.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly prefigures today's VR/AR platforms and 'metaverse' efforts (Meta's Horizon Worlds, VRChat, Fortnite/Roblox social spaces, Apple Vision Pro), built on real advances in head-mounted displays, real-time 3D rendering, and networked persistent-world server architecture.
rows.investmentNote: Meta, Microsoft, and others have invested tens of billions in metaverse/VR platforms, though mainstream adoption has lagged expectations.

rows.purpose: Used for long-distance messaging and tactical briefings, most famously Princess Leia's recorded holographic plea to Obi-Wan.
rows.realWorldBenefit: True volumetric holograms would enable far more natural remote meetings, telepresence, and 3D data visualization than flat video calls.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Current research into volumetric displays, light-field projection, and augmented-reality holography (e.g. Looking Glass displays, AR headsets) is progressing toward glasses-free 3D projection.
rows.investmentNote: Volumetric/holographic display companies (Looking Glass Factory, Light Field Lab) have real but modest funding compared to flat-panel/VR displays.

rows.purpose: Standard sidearm and rifle technology used by soldiers, bounty hunters, and troopers throughout the galaxy.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Directed-energy weapons could offer precision, reduced logistics (no physical ammunition), and tunable non-lethal settings for defense and security.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Directly paralleled by real directed-energy weapon research, including the U.S. Navy's shipboard laser weapon systems used against drones and small boats.
rows.investmentNote: US military directed-energy weapon programs (lasers, microwave weapons) are active but not yet man-portable rifle-scale.

rows.purpose: An alien-engineered self-replicating nanotech/biotech agent, seeded on Earth billions of years ago and later weaponized by Protogen, that hijacks and restructures biological matter to build interstellar infrastructure.
rows.realWorldBenefit: A safe, controllable version of programmable matter/nanotechnology could enable self-assembling structures, medical nanobots for cellular repair, and rapid large-scale construction.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Reflects real molecular nanotechnology and synthetic biology research (programmable matter, DNA origami, engineered self-replicating biomaterials) — currently far more limited and controllable than the protomolecule's runaway behavior.
rows.investmentNote: Only loosely analogous to real programmable-matter/self-assembling nanotech research; the specific alien bioengineering concept has no real analog.

rows.purpose: After each story cycle, hosts have their memories erased and behavior reset to original programming so parks can be replayed indefinitely for new guests.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Controlled memory management in AI systems could allow safe experimentation, rollback of harmful learned behaviors, and repeatable testing environments.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Corresponds to real techniques like model checkpointing/rollback and machine 'unlearning' research aimed at selectively removing learned data from AI models.
rows.investmentNote: Model checkpointing and controlled rollback of AI system state/behavior is standard current ML engineering practice, though not literal embodied memory-wipe.

venture.wedge: Machine-unlearning/model-rollback compliance tool removing specific training data from deployed AI models (GDPR right-to-be-forgotten)
venture.whoPays: Enterprises deploying AI subject to GDPR/data-privacy compliance

rows.namedIncumbents: Hirundo ($8M seed Jun 2025 led by Maverick Ventures Israel; machine unlearning for GDPR/copyright/bias without retraining, HPE partner ecosystem; prnewswire.com); Goodfire ($200M total; Ember API advertises unlearning hazardous behaviors; goodfire.com); Google Research (published auditing framework for machine unlearning, research not product; research.google)
rows.scene: At the end of a violent loop, a technician wipes a host's memory back to her baseline personality profile in the cold basement labs, resetting her for the next morning's guests as if the day's massacre never happened.

rows.purpose: Machine-built robotic hunters that patrol the real world's tunnels and destroy any human resistance or unshielded hovercraft they detect.
rows.realWorldBenefit: Autonomous multi-limbed robots capable of navigating harsh, unstructured environments could perform search-and-rescue or hazardous inspection work.
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels ongoing development of autonomous legged/multi-appendage robots (Boston Dynamics-style platforms) and military interest in autonomous drone swarms for reconnaissance and interdiction.
rows.investmentNote: Autonomous weapons systems and loitering munitions are a major, well-funded and controversial area of real military R&D investment.

venture.wedge: Autonomous legged-robot navigation software for hazardous-environment inspection (mines, disaster sites)

rows.scene: A squid-like Sentinel drops into Zion's tunnels and rips into the Nebuchadnezzar's hull, hunting the crew by heat and motion with no human operator directing it.

rows.purpose: Preserve knowledge and gatekeep access to sensitive research across centuries
rows.realWorldBenefit: Durable knowledge-preservation and persistent AI-agent capability
rows.howItCouldBeBuilt: Parallels holographic-projection technology combined with persistent autonomous AI-agent research
rows.investmentNote: Persistent autonomous AI agents combined with holographic projection draw on active but separate research streams.

venture.wedge: AI-curated long-term digital-archive access-control system for institutional/corporate historical records
